items.title: Rural allocation issue won't strain PH-BN ties, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: LUMUT: Differences of opinion over Rural and Regional Development Ministry allocations under the Finance Ministry will not affect Pakatan Harapan-Barisan Nasional political ties. Kamil, who is political secretary to the finance minister, said Finance Ministry-level discussions will review allocation requirements and prioritise high-impact rural development projects. It followed remarks by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, concerning payment delays for contractors handling projects under his ministry.

items.title: Zahid gives Rauf mandate to negotiate BN's Melaka election partnerships
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has given Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh the mandate to negotiate cooperation with any party for the upcoming Melaka state election. Zahid said any chosen partner must be sincere and honest to ensure BN continues to lead the state administration in the next term. In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won 5 and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured 2.

items.title: Gua Musang police: Six hikers feared missing after entering forest via Lojing and not emerging in Perak
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 6 — Six individuals — four family members and two mountain guides — who entered a forest area through Pos Dakoh, Lojing, Gua Musang on August 29 are feared missing after not leaving at Pos Kemar, Perak as scheduled on September 3. Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said family members of the hikers lodged a police report in Selangor today after they failed to return from their hike on the set date, adding that checks with the Forestry Department showed that the last contact with the group revealed that they were in the forest area in Perak. “For now, we are dealing with the Perak authorities to secure confirmation as based on their last contact, they were in Perak and no longer in Kelantan,” he said when contacted today, adding that the group had permits to enter the forest and engaged the services of two mountain guides.

items.title: Trump envoys arrive in Kyiv for first Ukraine visit
items.summary: KYIV: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Kyiv Sunday for their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, a day after holding talks with Russia's Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin on ending more than four years of war between the neighbours. US President Donald Trump's business partner Witkoff and son-in-law Kushner had visited Moscow several times but had not held talks in Kyiv – hit by deadly Russian strikes since 2022. An AFP reporter in Kyiv saw the American envoys arrive by train.

items.title: Study causes of Old Klang Road jams before building flyover, says expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A transport policy expert has urged Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Public Works Department (PWD) to diagnose the causes of congestion along Old Klang Road before deciding whether to build a proposed double-decker road or flyover. MY Mobility Vision founder and senior adviser Wan Agyl Wan Hassan was responding to Seputeh member of parliament Teresa Kok's call for DBKL and PWD to study the need for additional road capacity along the busy Kuala Lumpur corridor. he said.

items.title: Police confirm shooting of wanted drug suspect in Seremban housing area
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 6 — Police confirmed a local man suspected of drug-related activities was shot dead in a residential area in Garden Homes here early this afternoon. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the incident occurred at 1.50pm. “Yes, I confirm the incident,” he told reporters here today.

items.title: Man suspected of drug activities shot dead in Seremban
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A man suspected of involvement in drug-related activities was shot dead in a residential area in Garden Homes here early this afternoon. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the incident occurred at 1.50pm. "Yes, I confirm the incident," he told reporters here today.

items.title: [UPDATED] Former Felda-linked body general manager among two arrested over land irregularities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A former general manager of a statutory body linked to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), who holds the title Datuk, is one of two people arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over alleged irregularities involving the sale of land belonging to the statutory body. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrests. Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said issues involving a Felda subsidiary would be exposed within the next few weeks.

items.title: Don’t be deceived by RM2,500 deposit scam involving unofficial Kampung Jelutong SPK house offers, warns Jepak rep
items.summary: BINTULU, Sept 6 — The public have been warned against falling victim to unofficial offers to purchase houses in the Kampung Jelutong Village Expansion Scheme (SPK) in Jepak. Jepak assemblyman Iskandar Turkee said he had been informed about certain parties offering housing units in the area through unofficial channels, with prospective buyers reportedly being asked to pay a RM2,500 deposit. Handout photo shows one of the two housing models available at the Kampung Jelutong SPK.

items.title: Gerakan Youth urges party to draw clear line against extremism
items.summary: Speaking at the party's delegates' conference, Penang Gerakan Youth chief Tan Zhen Zune said Gerakan could work with any party, but must maintain its principles and draw a clear line against extremism. he said. he said.

items.title: Selangor ready to distribute face masks in worst‑hit haze areas, with priority for vulnerable groups, says exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — The Selangor Disaster Management Committee is ready to distribute face masks to the public and civil servants to cope with the ongoing haze situation. State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the distribution would focus on areas recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Selangor, particularly targeting vulnerable groups. “The public is also advised to reduce strenuous outdoor activities and remain indoors if air quality is unhealthy, while staying updated on the latest API readings in their respective areas,” she added.

items.title: Seven UiTM students remain under treatment after heat‑related incident; outdoor endurance events called off
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — Seven Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) students are still receiving treatment and undergoing medical monitoring following a heat-related incident while taking part in an endurance event in Pahang on Friday. In a statement today, UiTM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin said the university management was paying particular attention to the health and welfare of all the affected students, who are being treated at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (HOSHAS) in Temerloh and Jengka Hospital. “The five other students at Jengka Hospital are Nur Nabihah Musyidah Md Nasri (Johor branch, Segamat Campus), Nur Alia Farhana Abdul Fattah (Pahang branch, Jengka Campus), Muhamad Adam Azfar Suzaini and Muhammad Anas Shahrul Nizat from the Johor branch, as well as Izzharith Zafran Muhammad Zulkarnain from the Pahang branch,” he said.

items.title: US interference claim: 'One side may be lying' – Kamil Munim
items.summary: LUMUT: PKR Youth has urged authorities to investigate a claim by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang that the United States had offered assistance to the party to topple the Barisan Nasional government under former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. Its chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said the contradiction between Hadi's claim and the US Embassy's denial showed the matter was serious and warranted an investigation. Hadi said the question was raised after two senior Pas leaders, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Datuk Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, had earlier met the US ambassador.

items.title: Air quality deteriorates, 35 areas record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality deteriorated across several parts of the country this evening, with 35 monitoring stations recording unhealthy or very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today. Data released by the Department of Environment (DoE) on Facebook showed that one station recorded a very unhealthy API reading, while another 34 stations were classified as unhealthy. Overall, 29 stations recorded moderate air quality, while three stations recorded good air quality.

items.title: UiTM student's death during endurance challenge: Lab analysis pending
items.summary: MARAN: The post-mortem findings on the death of a Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) student who collapsed at the UiTM Jengka campus on Sept 4 are pending laboratory analysis. Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21, died at the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) in Temerloh at 2.08pm yesterday. Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the victim, who was from UiTM Seremban, Negri Sembilan, was taken to Jengka Hospital with eight other participants after experiencing breathing difficulties at 9.57pm.

items.title: Police open two probes after toddler mauled by five stray dogs
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Police have opened two investigation papers after a 2-year-old girl was severely injured in an attack by five stray dogs at Kampung Tambak in Peserai here yesterday. He said the investigation was initiated after police received a report from the hospital regarding a child undergoing treatment for severe injuries. "Preliminary investigations by the district Criminal Investigation Department found the incident occurred at 7am yesterday in front of the victim's family home in Peserai.

items.title: [UPDATED] Zahid says "blue wave" will recur in upcoming Melaka polls
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The "blue wave" phenomenon, intensified by the political understanding between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional that previously swept the Johor and Negri Sembilan polls, could be repeated in the upcoming Melaka election, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. "When the big day (Melaka polling day) arrives to determine the future of Melaka, do not forget that the blue wave that happened in Johor and Negri Sembilan will also reach Melaka," he said when closing the Melaka Youth Carnival X Jom Heboh at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today. Also present was Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

items.title: After heatwaves, will EU pivot back to the climate fight?
items.summary: IS climate change set for a comeback as a top EU priority, after a deadly summer of record-breaking heatwaves across Europe? The fight against global warming is expected to feature prominently in a key policy speech by EU chief Ursula von der Leyen this month, after two years critics say were marked by major environmental rollbacks. EU sources say von der Leyen will focus on "climate resilience" and the economic potential of green industries – two low-hanging fruits.

items.title: Hunting team records nine crocodiles captured in four‑day Kuala Baram operation
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 6 — The crocodile-hunting team ‘Eric Cat’ has recorded the capture of nine reptiles throughout their four-day operation in Kuala Baram, which kicked off on September 2. Team spokesman Eric Chong Fook Shin said the last catch was made last night, which was a 14-foot (over 4 metres) crocodile. Chong said the 14-foot crocodile was the team’s largest catch during their Kuala Baram operation.

items.title: Zulkifli: Higher allocations show Madani govt commitment as Malaysia earns global Islamic recognition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Madani Government remains committed to strengthening Islamic affairs in Malaysia through increased funding and efforts that have helped the country achieve global recognition in several areas. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the increase in allocation for Islamic affairs from RM1.5 billion in 2023 to RM2.6 billion this year reflected the government’s commitment to advancing the sector. Zulkifli said the government would continue developing the Islamic affairs agenda within the framework of the law while upholding respect for diversity and differences in society The PMK programme, an initiative by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) and agencies under Religious Affairs, aims to bring government services closer to the people through information-sharing, engagement and various community services.

items.title: Selangor to close schools if API exceeds 200 as haze worsens
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor will close schools, kindergartens, and childcare centres if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200, according to state authorities. State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the Selangor Education Department will continue to monitor API readings at school locations and take appropriate action based on pollution levels. "For the education sector, schools, kindergartens, and childcare centres must comply with prevailing regulations based on API readings.

items.title: Iran establishes 'economic war headquarters' amid US conflict, sanctions
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Iran's Economy Ministry has established an "economic war headquarters" to coordinate and accelerate responses to economic problems arising from wartime conditions, Deputy Economy Minister Morteza Zamanian said Sunday. Zamanian told the Tasnim news agency that the body would initially focus on issues falling within the ministry's responsibilities and authorities, Anadolu Ajansi reported. For issues extending beyond the ministry's authority, Zamanian said the ministry would use its role in broader economic policymaking, including through the government's economic commission and economic headquarters, to coordinate among institutions and pursue solutions at higher levels.

items.title: Ministry to assist MACC probe, act against Baja 3 supplier, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry will take action against the supplier of Additional Paddy Compound Fertiliser 3 (Baja 3) after it failed to meet its delivery commitments, said its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said the supplier's failure had caused delays in the delivery of fertiliser to padi farmers in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) area. He said the ministry would provide full cooperation to MACC to ensure all issues surrounding the supply process were properly clarified.

items.title: Don’t link salvation in the hereafter to politics, says religious affairs minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Differences in political support should not lead to a punitive or condescending attitude towards others, let alone linking salvation in the hereafter to membership of or support for any political organisation. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the determination of heaven and hell is the absolute right of Allah SWT and cannot be guaranteed by any individual, leader or political organisation. He said support for any political organisation was not a measure of attaining the pleasure of Allah SWT, as faith, piety and righteous deeds based on the Quran and Sunnah served as the primary foundations.

items.title: Monaco probes top lawyer amid long-running property corruption scandal
items.summary: MONACO: A top lawyer and senior adviser to Monaco's Prince Albert II was brought before a judge on Saturday amid a lengthy probe by investigators into a long-running scandal involving corruption and influence-peddling. Lawyer Thierry Lacoste, a former school friend and adviser to Albert, was taken into police custody on Wednesday as officials investigate a massive property project that fell through, the Monaco Public Prosecutor's Office said, reported German news agency dpa. The judge opened formal criminal proceedings against him on suspicion of forming a criminal organisation, actively bribing a national public official, passively exerting undue influence and money laundering.

items.title: Sri Aman only area with very unhealthy API reading of 216 as of 4pm, with no hazardous readings nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — No area recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading due to the haze as of 4 pm today, although Sri Aman in Sarawak was the only area to record a very unhealthy reading of 216. The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal reported unhealthy API readings in 35 other areas nationwide, moderate readings in 27 areas and good readings in four areas. Sarawak remained the worst-hit state, with 11 areas recording unhealthy air quality, namely Samalaju (196), Samarahan (196), Kuching (191), Bintulu (190), Mukah (188), Sarikei (185), IPD Serian (182), ILP Miri (176), Sibu (174), Miri (170) and Limbang (157).

items.title: Rescued Malayan tiger Yong Choh released into Tasik Kenyir national park
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A female Malayan tiger rescued from Kampung Choh in Sungai Siput, Perak, on July 22 has been released into its natural habitat at Terengganu National Park in Tasik Kenyir. "Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup officiated the Wildlife Transfer Barge and Release Ceremony at Terengganu National Park, Tasik Kenyir yesterday, as part of efforts to strengthen wildlife conservation and manage human-wildlife conflicts," the ministry said in a statement today. Other wildlife released under the programme include black panthers, sambar deer, barking deer, pangolins, common palm civets, mouse deer, and greater mouse deer.

items.title: Anak Krakatau eruption leaves Indonesian worker stranded at KLIA
items.summary: SEPANG: An Indonesian domestic worker's plans to return to Jakarta were disrupted after her flight was cancelled following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport due to volcanic ash from the eruption of Anak Krakatau. The disruption affected 209 flights and 22,798 passengers, according to reports. Yati Rasta, 61, said she arrived at the airport as early as 6am today to catch her 11am flight to Jakarta.

items.title: Budget 2027 to emphasise support for M40 and lower‑income groups, says Finance Minister’s aide
items.summary: LUMUT, Sept 6 — Budget 2027 is expected to place particular emphasis on efforts to address socioeconomic issues, including the welfare of the middle-income (M40) and lower-income groups, according to an aide of the Finance Minister. Anwar, who is Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on October 9. Muhammad Kamil said existing initiatives such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened to ease the financial burden on households.

items.title: UiTM duathlon: 9 participants experience breathing difficulties, 1 dies
items.summary: KUANTAN: Nine Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) participants, including a 21-year-old male student who died yesterday, experienced breathing difficulties during the duathlon event on Sept 4. The student, Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21, died at the intensive care unit (ICU) of Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) in Temerloh at 2.08pm yesterday. Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said two students remained admitted to Hoshas' ICU, while six others were receiving treatment at Jengka Hospital.

items.title: Doctors induce coma for Batu Pahat toddler wounded in stray dog attack
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 6 — A two-year-old girl is fighting for her life after being critically injured by a pack of five stray dogs outside her grandmother’s house in Kampung Tambak, Sungai Kelambu, Peserai in Batu Pahat yesterday. Darlinda said she found the front door open after taking a bath and saw the dogs attacking the girl outside the house. The girl was later transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital here because of the severity of her injuries, Darlinda said.

items.title: Six, including family of four, feared missing during Gunung Gerah hike
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: Six people, including a family of four, are feared missing after joining the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah in the Lojing Permanent Forest Reserve here. The group, comprising a married couple, their two children, and two mountain guides, began their trek on Aug 29. District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo confirmed receiving the report.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia strengthen intelligence-sharing to combat cross-border drug syndicates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Indonesia are strengthening intelligence-sharing and joint enforcement efforts as drug syndicates increasingly operate across borders and employ more complex methods to evade the authorities. NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan chaired the Malaysian delegation, while the Indonesian delegation was led by Dittipidnarkoba director Brigadier-General Eko Hadi Santoso. Hussein said both sides also shared updates on the investigation involving the Malaysian airline second officer arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 29.

items.title: Anwar and old friend Al Gore reunite (virtually) to talk climate challenges, decades after ‘reformasi’
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he spoke with former US vice-president Al Gore about the global climate crisis, haze affecting Malaysia and the country’s transition towards cleaner energy. Anwar said Gore, who was in Singapore, had expressed sympathy over the haze after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian, Sarawak exceeded 500 two days ago. Anwar said they also discussed the wider effects of climate change, including the recent floods in Nepal.

items.title: Fadhlina praises Taanusiya’s Miss World showing and her commitment to education advocacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has praised Taanusiya Chetty, who finished third in the Miss World 2026 pageant, for championing education and advocacy as part of her cause. “I am impressed not only by her achievement on the world stage, but also by Taanusiya’s commitment to making education and advocacy part of her cause. “Congratulations, Taanusiya.

items.title: Fadhlina praises Taanusiya for championing education, advocacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has praised Taanusiya Chetty for championing education and advocacy after the Malaysian beauty queen finished third at the Miss World 2026 pageant. "I am impressed not only by her achievement on the world stage, but also by Taanusiya's commitment to making education and advocacy part of her cause. "Congratulations, Taanusiya.

items.title: Malaysians stranded in Jakarta as Anak Krakatau eruption grounds flights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, which spewed volcanic ash across parts of Indonesia, has disrupted flight operations, particularly at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten. Among them was Threads user Spritzerphilips, who was stuck at the airport when her scheduled flight was affected today. An hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight on Tuesday.

items.title: Youth and Sports Ministry to prioritise grassroots sports development and athlete welfare in Budget 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — The Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS) has submitted an initial framework of its Budget 2027 proposals to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration, with grassroots sports development, youth participation and athletes’ welfare among the ministry’s priorities. Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the framework was prepared based on input gathered through the Madani Youth Budget Tour being conducted in six zones nationwide. “Although all the tour sessions have not been completed, KBS has obtained various views from youth organisations, sports associations as well as unorganised youths for review and assessment.

items.title: 'Unsustainable burden': PPP calls for urgent solution to public hospital doctor shortage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government must urgently address the chronic shortage of doctors, medical officers (MOs) and specialists in government hospitals, the People's Progressive Party (PPP) said. Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said manpower shortages and the uneven distribution of healthcare personnel were contributing to excessive workloads, longer waiting times, burnout and delays in specialist treatment, with Sabah and Sarawak facing particularly serious challenges. He said the government must accelerate the abolition of the contract system, provide sufficient permanent positions, fill vacant posts, increase specialist training capacity and address the uneven distribution of doctors.

items.title: Heavy traffic builds on major highways as holidaymakers head home
items.summary: The Malaysian Highway Authority's (MHA) Traffic Management Centre (TMC) said traffic was moving slowly along several stretches of the North-South Expressway (NSE), New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) and Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway as of 2.55pm today. On the northbound NSE, slow-moving traffic was reported from the Senawang lay-by towards Port Dickson, Bangi to Kajang, and after the Sungai Besi toll plaza towards the city centre. On the North-South Expressway Central Link (Elite), northbound traffic was slow from Putrajaya towards Bandar Saujana Putra.

items.title: Anak Krakatau chaos strands Malaysians in Jakarta, with hotels full and next flights two days away
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 6 — Malaysians stranded in Jakarta after volcanic ash from the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted flights are now scrambling for alternative arrangements, with some travellers facing delays of several days before they can return home. One traveller who goes by the moniker Spritzerphilips on Threads was a picture of fatigue and anxiety after being stranded at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after her flight, scheduled for today, was cancelled. About an hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight for Tuesday.

items.title: Water supply to 34,000 accounts in Machang expected to be restored tomorrow after pipe repairs
items.summary: MACHANG, Sept 6 — Water supply to about 34,000 consumer accounts in Machang, southern Kota Bharu and parts of Pasir Puteh is expected to be restored in stages from noon tomorrow following a main pipe leak in Pulai Chondong here. Kelantan Public Works, Infrastructure, Water and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Dr Izani Husin said the leak in the 1,100-millimetre glass-fibre reinforced plastic (GRP) pipe was detected on Friday, with excavation and repair works beginning on the same day. Meanwhile, AKSB head of Production Dr Mohd Hilmi P. Ramli said the company planned to replace the GRP pipe with mild steel pipes following the fourth leak since it was commissioned eight years ago.

items.title: Japan releases tips on bear spray use amid concern over attacks
items.summary: TOKYO: The Japanese government recently released guidelines on how to check the specifications of bear repellent sprays and properly choose and use them amid a proliferation of ineffective products on the market, Kyodo News reported. With public interest in bear sprays growing as the country faces an increase in bear sightings and attacks, the Environment Ministry and the Consumer Affairs Agency have urged manufacturers and distributors to provide information on the efficacy of their products. "Some products rebranded for bears were actually made for use against people," said Shinjiro Sasaki, a ministry official who also recommended that people practice using the repellents.

items.title: FT mufti: ‘Religious exploitation’ more accurate term, not ‘riding on religion’, to describe misuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The term ‘religious exploitation’ is more appropriate and objective than ‘riding on religion’ to describe the act of misusing religion for worldly interests, said Federal Territories Mufti Ahmad Fauwaz Fadzil. He said the term ‘riding on religion’ should not be used indiscriminately as it could lead to generalisations about religious figures, including scholars and preachers who sincerely champion the cause of Islam. The term ‘religious exploitation’ focuses more specifically on the act of misusing religion to gain wealth, influence or position, while also more clearly illustrating the existence of those who take advantage and those who are deceived.

items.title: More money for Agriculture Ministry? Anwar says maybe — if the books stay clean, so farmers won’t suffer
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security could receive a bigger allocation in Budget 2027, provided the ministry continues to uphold good governance. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said additional funding could be considered as long as the ministry ensured that public money was managed properly and reached farmers, fishermen and paddy planters. Speaking to reporters later, Mohamad who is better known as Mat Sabu, said the additional allocation is to allow his ministry to prepare early for potential challenges next year.

items.title: At flood-destroyed China-Nepal border, no sign of a once-busy port
items.summary: ABOUT 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China's main border crossing with Nepal. The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on Aug 26. Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood.

items.title: Kedah appeals for continued cloud seeding as Pedu, Muda and Ahning dam levels keep falling
items.summary: He said before cloud seeding on Sept 2, total water supply at the Pedu, Muda and Ahning Dams stood at 37.14 per cent, but had dropped to 36.64 per cent this morning. “The water level at Pedu Dam is now at 38.46 per cent, compared to 39.02 per cent on Sept 2, while Muda Dam recorded 9.04 per cent, down from 9.32 per cent previously,” he told Bernama today. Meanwhile, supply at Ahning Dam stood at 45.00 per cent, compared to 45.32 per cent over the same period.

items.title: Police step up highway monitoring as motorists return home after school holidays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are closely monitoring major highways nationwide as motorists begin making their way home following the school holidays. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said highway patrol units were on the ground monitoring traffic conditions and ensuring the safety of road users. Hasbullah reminded motorists not to rush despite potentially heavier traffic and longer travelling times.

items.title: Komuniti Madani must be stronger bridge between government and people, says Wan Azizah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Komuniti Madani initiative should play a greater role as a bridge between the government and the people, Bandar Tun Razak member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said. "Do not merely be information transmitters; be attentive listeners to the issues affecting the elderly, families in distress and the needs of the youth," she said at the Komuniti Madani appointment certificate ceremony for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency here today. Also present were the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad, and Bandar Tun Razak Komuniti Madani chairman Jonathan Vela.

items.title: Bukit Lagi Hindu temple row: Perlis police get two more days to detain activist as probe widens into criminal trespass
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 6 — The remand of a 55-year-old activist detained over social media posts linked to a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple in Bukit Lagi has been extended by two days as police pursue a separate criminal trespass investigation. Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor allowed the police application today for the extension, with the activist being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code, Harian Metro reported today. Police had said the posts included a picture promoting the Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali gathering, which was held at the temple site on August 30.

items.title: Fadhlina pledges no SJKT closures as RM12.6m Sungai Bakap Tamil school project gets going after 17 years
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 6 — The government has assured that no Tamil vernacular school will be closed as construction finally begins on a RM12.6 million replacement building for SJKT Sungai Bakap after nearly 17 years of delays. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the Madani Government would instead continue to focus on the development and maintenance of all SJKT, as well as programmes to strengthen teachers and pupils. “We give an assurance that, under the Madani Government, no SJKT will be closed.

items.title: Volcanic ash grounds 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights by Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK). Malaysia Airlines said in its post on X that it would cancel 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Jakarta (CGK), namely MH713, MH712, MH711, MH710, MH717, MH716, MH721, MH720, MH723, MH722, MH725 and MH724. “Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers,” it said.

items.title: United Sikhs Malaysia head into Nepal’s worst-hit flood zone to help 98 kids whose parents are missing (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Five Malaysian volunteers are heading deep into one of Nepal’s worst-hit flood zones, travelling over rough terrain to deliver emergency supplies and help families whose homes and communities have been devastated by floods and landslides. The team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance, is travelling to Dhunche in Rasuwa district to establish a base camp before pushing on to Syapru Besi near the Nepal-Tibet border. https://www.facebook.com/UNITEDSIKHSMALAYSIA/videos/06092026-mission-update-nepal-flood-reliefunited-sikhs-malaysias-team-a-is-curre/3827014714104717/ United Sikhs Malaysia’s mission comes as other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster.

items.title: Zahid tells parties to park PM talk, focus on Melaka polls instead
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today urged political parties to put talk of who could become prime minister after the 16th general election aside for now, saying the focus should instead be on the upcoming Melaka state election. The Umno president said it was too early to name or discuss a potential prime ministerial candidate when the timing of Parliament’s dissolution and the next general election remained unknown, Harian Metro reported. Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said attention should remain on the Melaka election before any discussions on federal-level political matters take place.

items.title: Sarawak extends cloud‑seeding operations to tackle transboundary haze as Serian API shows improving trend
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 6 — Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow in an ongoing effort to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state. Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall over the targeted Bakun and Murum Dam areas. Sarawak has been conducting cloud-seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.

items.title: Chief Justice leads 128‑strong Terengganu honours list in conjunction with Sultan Mizan’s 64th birthday
items.summary: Also in attendance were his younger siblings, Tengku Seri Setia Mahkota Raja Tengku Datuk Seri Muhammad Muaz; Tengku Puteri Utama Raja Tengku Nadhirah Zahrah; and Tengku Puteri Daulath Raja Tengku Fatimatuz Zahra’. Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Seri Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk Seri. Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Setia Sultan Mizan Abidin Terengganu (D.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk, on Federal Court Judge Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and CelcomDigi Berhad board adviser and former chief executive officer Datuk Mohamad Idham Nawawi.

items.title: Two foreigners remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 6 — Two foreign nationals have been remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park last Thursday. Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) said both individuals were remanded for three days, from September 4 to September 7, to assist with the investigation. 27], which prohibits the taking or removal of plants from national park areas without permission from the controller of national parks and nature reserves.

items.title: Former minister’s remand extended two days in Tabung Haji RCI hotel‑lease probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The remand of a former minister detained over investigations into a Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) hotel‑lease issue in Saudi Arabia has been extended for two more days. According to Bernama, Magistrate Muhammad Bukhori Md Ruslan Zakariah issued the extension, which runs from tomorrow until Tuesday, after the Malaysian Anti‑Corruption Commission (MACC) applied for it at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning. MACC Chief Commissioner Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Anwar expresses solidarity with Indonesia over volcanic disaster and haze challenges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed solidarity with the people of Indonesia following the volcanic disaster and haze-related challenges currently facing the country. Anwar said he conveyed this when he contacted former Indonesian President Joko Widodo, better known as Jokowi, who is currently in Penang to attend the Penang Peace Dialogue. In a post on his Facebook page today, Anwar said the conversation also saw the two leaders exchange updates.

items.title: DOE monitors bush and peatland fires in Mukah, Daro in Sarawak amid dry spell
items.summary: DoE deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said based on the latest status, the fire in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area had been mostly controlled, covering an area of nine hectares. “However, the fire still affects approximately one hectare in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area and is currently being extinguished,” she said in a statement on Sunday. Meanwhile, Azuri said two air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am on Sunday.
